name: MAX690ACSA+T
title: MAX690A/MAX692A/MAX802L/MAX802M/MAX805L: microprocessor supervisors with battery backup, watchdog and power-fail comparator
summary: Five 8-pin supervisors for +5 V microprocessor systems. Each one holds a reset during power-up, power-down and brownout, switches CMOS RAM over to a backup battery when VCC fails, pulses reset if the 1.6 s watchdog is not serviced, and carries a 1.25 V comparator for early power-fail or low-battery warning. They differ in reset threshold (4.65 V or 4.40 V), reset polarity (MAX805L is active high) and power-fail accuracy (±2% on MAX802L/M). MAX690ACSA+T is the MAX690A, 0°C to +70°C, in the 8-pin SO, lead(Pb)-free.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Switched supply for CMOS RAM. Switched to VCC by an internal P-channel MOSFET while VCC is over the reset threshold; below it, fed from whichever of VCC and VBATT is higher.

pins.name: PFI
pins.function: Power-fail comparator input. PFO is driven low whenever PFI sits under 1.25 V. Tie to GND or VCC if the comparator is unused.

pins.name: PFO
pins.function: Power-fail comparator output, active low: low while PFI is under 1.25 V, high otherwise.

pins.name: WDI
pins.function: Watchdog input. Holding it at one level for the 1.6 s timeout lets the timer expire and fires a reset. Floating, or driven by a three-state buffer in its high-impedance state, it turns the watchdog off. The timer is cleared by any edge on WDI, by a reset, or by WDI going high-impedance.

pins.name: RESET
pins.function: Reset output, active low. Each trigger gives a 200 ms low pulse. Held low while VCC is under the reset threshold (4.65 V on MAX690A/MAX802L, 4.4 V on MAX692A/MAX802M) and for 200 ms after VCC climbs back above it; a watchdog timeout also fires it.

pins.name: VBATT
pins.function: Backup battery input. Once VCC is under the reset threshold, VBATT takes over VOUT if it is 20 mV above VCC; VOUT goes back to VCC when VCC rises 20 mV above VBATT. The 40 mV hysteresis stops chatter on a slowly falling VCC.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit
circuits.description: MAX690A or MAX802L supervising a microprocessor and its CMOS RAM. A divider from the unregulated input feeds PFI, so PFO drives the processor's NMI as the raw supply sags. RESET goes to the processor's reset, an I/O line toggles WDI, and the RAM runs from VOUT, backed by a 3.6 V lithium cell on VBATT.
notes: R1 and R2 set the PFI trip point; no values are given.
BUS is the processor's data and address bus to the RAM.

circuits.title: SuperCap backup with a +5V ±5% supply
circuits.description: A 0.1 F SuperCap on VBATT, charged from +5 V through one diode, stands in for the backup battery on MAX690A, MAX802L or MAX805L. VOUT feeds static RAM; the reset output goes to the processor.
notes: On MAX805L the reset output is the active-high RESET.

circuits.title: SuperCap backup with a +5V ±10% supply
circuits.description: MAX692A or MAX802M with a 0.1 F SuperCap charged from +5 V through two diodes in series, with 100 kΩ from the middle node to ground, so the SuperCap stops near VCC - 0.5 V. VOUT feeds static RAM; RESET goes to the processor.

circuits.title: Power-fail comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: R1 and R2 divide VIN onto PFI; R3 from PFO back to PFI adds hysteresis, so PFO falls at VL and rises at VH around VTRIP. The optional C1 on PFI filters noise. PFO goes to the processor.
notes: Misprint: MAX690 in the part names should read MAX690A.

circuits.title: Monitoring a negative voltage
circuits.description: A divider from +5 V (R1) to the negative rail V- (R2) sets PFI; PFO stays low while V- is well below its trip point VTRIP and goes high as V- rises above it.

circuits.title: Interfacing to a processor with bidirectional reset I/O
circuits.description: A 4.7 kΩ series resistor between the supervisor's active-low RESET and the processor's bidirectional reset pin lets the processor pull its own reset low without contention. A buffer on the processor side passes the reset on to the rest of the system.

operation.text: From VCC = 1 V upward RESET is held low. When VCC passes the reset threshold RESET stays low for one internally timed reset pulse width (200 ms typ), then goes high. A dip of VCC under the threshold re-triggers reset; if it lands during a pulse already running, the pulse restarts and lasts another 200 ms. Falling, RESET is held low from the threshold down to VCC = 1 V.

If WDI sees no rising or falling edge for 1.6 s, RESET pulses low. The timer stays cleared, and does not count, while reset is asserted or WDI is left open; it starts counting as soon as reset ends or WDI is driven to either level, so after a reset the processor has 1.6 s to service it. Pulses down to 50 ns are recognised. With WDI held at a fixed level, reset pulses repeat every 1.8 s (tWD plus tRS).
MAX805L is MAX690A with the reset output inverted: RESET is active high and is valid down to VCC = 1.1 V, for processors such as the 80C51 that want a high reset.

PFI is compared against an internal 1.25 V reference; under it, PFO goes low. The comparator stands apart from the rest of the chip. A typical use divides down the unregulated input of the +5 V regulator onto PFI, with the ratio set so PFI crosses 1.25 V just before the regulator drops out; PFO then interrupts the processor so it can prepare for power loss. In battery-backup mode PFO is held low and the comparator powered down to save battery current.

With VCC over the reset threshold, VOUT is fed from VCC through a 5Ω PMOS switch. Below the threshold, VOUT is fed from whichever of VCC and VBATT is higher; from VBATT the path is an 80Ω switch. Unlike MAX690/MAX692, all five parts join VBATT to VOUT only when VCC is under the reset threshold and VBATT is above VCC; VBATT above VCC alone is not enough. Above the reset threshold VCC is tied to the substrate whatever VBATT is, and diode D1 between VBATT and the substrate conducts from VBATT into VCC once VBATT is 0.6 V or more above VCC.

In backup mode the internal circuits run from the battery. With VCC just under VBATT the battery supplies about 30 µA typ; once VCC is more than 1 V below VBATT the switchover comparator turns off and the drain falls under 1 µA.

A SuperCap (around 0.1 F) can replace the battery. Its voltage must stay no more than 0.6 V above the maximum reset threshold. With a diode from VCC (Figure 4) it charges quickly to a diode drop under VCC and, through diode leakage, slowly up to VCC, so with MAX690A/MAX802L/MAX805L VCC must not exceed 5.35 V. For a ±10% supply, MAX692A or MAX802M with the two-diode circuit of Figure 5 charges the SuperCap to VCC - 0.5 V: 5.0 V at VCC = 5.5 V, 0.5 V above the maximum reset threshold.

Single lithium cells of 3.0 V to 3.6 V open-circuit voltage suit the backup role, given their low self-discharge and high energy density. A battery whose open-circuit voltage is under the minimum reset threshold plus 0.3 V connects straight to VBATT with no other parts. A higher-voltage battery cannot serve, because current flows into the substrate through D1 when VCC is near the reset threshold.
Without a backup source, VBATT goes to ground and VOUT is joined to VCC. VOUT then needs no switching, and the direct link avoids the switch drop that could leave VOUT under VCC.

The battery can be taken out while VCC is good without causing a reset: backup mode cannot begin while VCC is above the reset threshold. Parts that enter backup whenever VBATT nears VCC can instead be reset falsely by leakage charge collecting on an open VBATT pin.

Feedback from PFO through R3 gives the comparator hysteresis, so it does not chatter when VIN hovers at the trip point. R1 and R2 set PFI to 1.25 V at VTRIP; R3 is usually about ten times R1 or R2. Keep at least 1 µA in R1 and R2 so the 25 nA max PFI current does not move the trip point, and keep R3 above 10 kΩ so PFO is not loaded. The optional C1 adds noise rejection.

With R1 from +5 V to PFI and R2 from PFI to the negative rail, PFO is low while the rail is strongly negative and goes high as it rises toward ground. Accuracy depends on the PFI threshold tolerance, the VCC level and the resistors.

A processor with a bidirectional reset pin, such as the 68HC11, can fight the active-low RESET output: if RESET drives high while the processor pulls low, the level is undefined. A 4.7 kΩ resistor between RESET and the processor's reset pin solves it; other circuits that need reset take it through a buffer.
Die size 0.078 in (1.98 mm) by 0.061 in (1.55 mm), 573 transistors. Pads: VCC, VOUT, VBATT, RESET, WDI, GND, PFI, PFO. The substrate is left unconnected.
